original_question: Can you recover certain derivatives of the Levi form at a weakly pseudoconvex point in terms of the weighted boundary behavior of the Kobayashi metric?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, as sharpened by Proposition 1.2 and proved for h-extendible boundary points by Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s core theme: relating weighted boundary asymptotics of the Kobayashi metric near a weakly pseudoconvex boundary point to the local Levi geometry, i.e. to the Levi invariants encoded by a model polynomial.
missing_details: The paper is not about an arbitrary weakly pseudoconvex point; the precise proved result is for a C^∞-smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^n at an h-extendible finite-type boundary point ξ0.
The paper treats the generalized Kobayashi-Royden metrics F^k, for every integer k ≥ 1; the ordinary Kobayashi metric is only the case k = 1.

The relevant local data are not described vaguely as “certain derivatives of the Levi form”; they are encoded by the weighted homogeneous plurisubharmonic polynomial P in Catlin-type normal coordinates, which the paper treats as the precise Levi invariant/model object.
One must specify the Catlin multitype (1,m2,…,mn) and the associated weight vector Λ = (1/m2,…,1/mn).

A local defining function must be put in the form ρ(z1,z′) = Re z1 + P(z′) + R(z), with P Λ-homogeneous, plurisubharmonic, and containing no pluriharmonic terms, and with R of strictly higher weighted order.
The approach to the boundary is not arbitrary: the limit is taken along sequences ηj → ξ0 inside a fixed nontangential cone.

The weighting is not just by boundary distance in words; it is implemented by the anisotropic dilation πt(z′) = (t^{1/m2}z2,…,t^{1/mn}zn), with ε(ηj) = |ρ(ηj)| ≈ dist(ηj,∂Ω), and with the tangent vector X rescaled by the induced map (π_{ε(ηj)})_*.
The limit depends on the scaled tangential location α = lim π_{1/ε(ηj)}(η′j), which your draft omits.

The limiting object is the generalized Kobayashi metric of the model domain M_{P,α} = {(w,z′) ∈ ℂ × ℂ^{n-1} : Re w + P(z′ + α) − P(α) < 0}, equivalently the metric of MP at the translated point (−1 − P(α), α).
The statement is quantified for every X ∈ ℂ^n and every k ≥ 1, and for every nontangential sequence with the stated scaled tangential limit α.

If one wants the simpler special case where the limit depends only on the complex normal component, one must additionally restrict to a narrower cone Γs with s > 1, for which α = 0; this is not automatic from your draft.

The paper’s official formulation is not a broad inverse problem asking whether one can reconstruct arbitrary derivatives from metric data; it asks for the precise weighted boundary limit and identifies it with the model metric determined by the Levi invariants.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded C^∞-smooth pseudoconvex domain, and let ξ0 ∈ ∂Ω be an h-extendible finite-type boundary point with Catlin multitype (1,m2,…,mn). In local holomorphic coordinates z = (z1,z′) centered at ξ0, assume a defining function has the form ρ(z) = Re z1 + P(z′) + R(z), where P is a Λ-homogeneous plurisubharmonic polynomial, Λ = (1/m2,…,1/mn), and P has no pluriharmonic terms. If ηj → ξ0 nontangentially, εj := |ρ(ηj)| ≈ dist(ηj,∂Ω), and π_{1/εj}(η′j) → α under the anisotropic dilation πt(z′) = (t^{1/m2}z2,…,t^{1/mn}zn), must one have, for every integer k ≥ 1 and every X ∈ ℂ^n, the weighted limit lim_{j→∞} F^k_Ω(ηj,(π_{εj})_*X) = F^k_{M_{P,α}}((-1,0′),X), equivalently F^k_{MP}((-1 − P(α),α),X), so that in particular for k = 1 the weighted nontangential boundary behavior of the ordinary Kobayashi metric is exactly governed by the Levi invariants encoded by P?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, with the same hypotheses and notation, one may ask whether lim_{j→∞} F^k_Ω(ηj,(π_{εj})_*X) = F^k_{MP}((-1 − P(α),α),X) for every X ∈ ℂ^n and k ≥ 1, since the paper identifies this with the model-domain formulation using M_{P,α}.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s introduction-level question about whether weighted boundary limits of the Kobayashi metric are determined by the local Levi geometry. The nearest paper-faithful formulation is not a free-form “recovery of derivatives” problem, but Conjecture 1.1: the weighted boundary limits should be described by the model attached to the Levi invariants. Proposition 1.2 supplies the precise h-extendible/model reformulation, and Theorem 1.3 is the paper’s affirmative result in that setting. The refined question therefore keeps the draft’s intent but replaces the vague phrase “certain derivatives of the Levi form” by the exact invariant object used in the paper, namely the weighted homogeneous model polynomial P and the associated model domain. This stays narrow, theorem-faithful, and does not broaden the paper into a general inverse problem. The paper’s introduction states the aim as understanding the precise relationship between weighted boundary limits and Levi invariants, and the later discussion makes clear that the h-extendible case is the large class for which the conjectured description is proved.
